title: Preventing SQL injection: parameterised queries and using an ORM correctly

videos.script: A receptionist searches for a patient called Lucia D'Ávila. The portal answers with an error. {{error}} Nobody attacked anything. A real surname has an apostrophe in it, and the code pasted the name into the middle of a SQL statement. {{pasted}} The database read the apostrophe as the end of a string. Then it tried to read the rest of her name as SQL. {{read}} That is the whole of SQL injection: data that reaches the database as code. The same mistake that breaks on an apostrophe obeys whoever types something worse. {{same}} The fix is not to strip apostrophes. It is to send the query and the values separately, so a value can never become code. {{separately}} Today a search, a sort and an ORM, each fixed with a test that keeps it fixed. {{today}}
